clue.text: One involved in the actual robbery

indicators.note: something involved in a thing is caught up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: 'the very' thing is the actual one, as in 'the very man I wanted'
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of taking part in the real robbery itself.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside THE VERY, after TH, to give THIEVERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Thievery is the act of stealing, a straightforward synonym for robbery.

clue.text: Prevent vessels capsizing

indicators.note: a capsizing boat turns upside down, so in a down entry the word is flipped end to end

blocks.note: pots are vessels for holding food or liquid

explanation.surface: An order to stop boats from overturning.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something happening is to prevent it; both verbs mean block or halt.

clue.text: Plump, but cold, spouse

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
hubby is an informal word for husband

explanation.surface: A description of a partner: well-padded, yet emotionally chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby and plump both describe someone pleasantly rounded or slightly overweight.

clue.text: Early present

blocks.note: first meaning: ahead of time
second meaning: to put forward or propose, as in advancing an idea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Early present' reads like a gift given before the birthday; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance booking is made early, and to advance a theory is to put it forward for consideration.

clue.text: Refuse marriage, perhaps, and security? It's high risk

blocks.note: junk is rubbish, refuse as a noun
marriage is an example of a bond between people, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a proposal and financial safety, a risky move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb meaning decline; it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A junk bond is a high-yield security with a poor credit rating, so investors run a large risk of default.

clue.text: Au fait with the ways of the City Road, wife is taking Ecstasy

definitions.text: Au fait with the ways of the City

blocks.note: a street is a road
W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: City Road is a London street; someone's wife there takes drugs and knows the urban scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City Road' reads as one London street name, but the definition ends at 'City'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone streetwise has the shrewd practical knowledge needed to get by in a tough urban environment.

clue.text: Islander in frenzied trance

indicators.note: frenzied means wild and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An island dweller has fallen into a wild, ecstatic trance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cretan is a native of Crete, the largest Greek island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Eaglet finally emerged from egg under straw

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, so only its closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of eaglet
a chick that has emerged from its egg has hatched

explanation.surface: A baby eagle at last breaks out of its egg in a straw nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under straw' looks like part of the nest scene, but it is the definition, describing a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A thatched cottage has a roof of straw or reeds, so it sits under straw.

clue.text: Absolute idiot loses head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: a nutter is slang for a crazy or foolish person

explanation.surface: A complete fool loses his temper or his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter and absolute are both intensifiers meaning complete or total, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: Man approaches politician for cannabis

blocks.note: he is the pronoun for a man
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A man approaches an MP to ask about drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approaches' tells us the man comes up to, and so sits next to, the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is the cannabis plant, grown for fibre as well as for the drug.

clue.text: Lake Chad, foul with TB and bubonic plague

indicators.note: foul here means messed up or spoiled, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An African lake is polluted and its people afflicted with tuberculosis and plague.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Death was the pandemic of bubonic plague that swept Europe in the fourteenth century.

clue.text: Money left in joint account? Unknown!

blocks.note: a leg is a joint of meat
AC is the abbreviation for account
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about cash left in a shared bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint account' reads as a shared bank account; joint is a cut of meat here.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is money or property left to someone in a will, a bequest.

clue.text: Police got a builder to show remorse

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining an adjective: to be apologetic is to show remorse

indicators.note: a builder constructs something new, so these letters are built into a fresh word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Officers arrested a tradesman to make him say sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: an apologetic person is one who shows remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Being apologetic means expressing regret or sorrow for a wrong, which is showing contrition.

clue.text: Pieces of toast with toppings - odd bits of carrot and some sturgeon - in Italy

indicators.note: the odd bits are those in odd-numbered positions, first, third and fifth
some means only part of the word is used, here its opening letters

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of carrot
the first two letters of sturgeon
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A menu description of Italian toasted canapés with carrot and fish on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Crostini are small slices of toasted bread topped with savoury morsels, an Italian appetiser.

clue.text: Darkly romantic revolutionary in Corby

indicators.note: something revolutionary overturns the established order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; Corby is a town in Northamptonshire

explanation.surface: A brooding romantic rebel is found in the English town of Corby.
explanation.definitionFit: Byronic describes the brooding, passionate, moody hero type associated with the poet Lord Byron.

clue.text: One starts to get nasty, or shout. It''s stupid

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, so each word gives its initial

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
the first letters of get, nasty and or
to rant is to shout angrily

explanation.surface: Someone begins to turn nasty or yell, and it is dumb behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant is used loosely to mean foolish or lacking knowledge, close to stupid.

clue.text: Junkies go on to say: "One gets caught by heartless traffickers"

indicators.note: with the heart cut out, only the outside edges of the word remain

blocks.note: to add is to go on to say something more
the Roman numeral for one
c stands for caught on a cricket scorecard
the outside letters of traffickers

explanation.surface: Drug users speak up, saying one of them was arrested by cruel dealers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets caught' looks like a container signal, but caught is just C, from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Junkies is slang for drug addicts, people dependent on heroin or similar substances.

clue.text: Film a cricketer

blocks.note: first meaning: the 1949 Carol Reed thriller starring Orson Welles
second meaning: a fielder placed behind the batsman on the off side

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, third man is a fielding position near the boundary behind the wicket, and the player stationed there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Third Man is a classic film noir, and the third man is the cricket fielder in that position.

clue.text: Rock star wed manager

indicators.note: to rock something is to shake it, so these letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock musician marries the band's manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock star' reads as one phrase, and solvers may think of Rod Stewart; rock is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward manages an estate, household or event on someone else's behalf.

clue.text: Drunk bound to get a drink

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters reel into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
to net something is to get or gain it

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy is sure to fetch another drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to'; the words are split, bound being the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubonnet is a French aperitif, a sweet fortified wine flavoured with quinine.

clue.text: University, which in France is one of a kind

blocks.note: uni is short for university
que is French for which or that

explanation.surface: A claim that a certain French university stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Unique means being the only one of its type, without equal or parallel.

clue.text: A male clumsily embracing single girl

indicators.note: done clumsily means done awkwardly and out of order, so the letters are muddled
embracing means hugging, so the jumbled letters wrap around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
I is one, a single unit

explanation.surface: An awkward man gives a hug to an unattached young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia is a female first name, and girl's names are commonly clued simply as girl.

clue.text: Dextrous, dizzy Dora has sex appeal

indicators.note: a dizzy head spins, so the letters are spun round into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
it is an old word for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A scatterbrained but skilful woman named Dora is attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and quick with the hands or mind, the same as dextrous.

clue.text: Doctor Ewing, oarsman and viticulturalist

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written
an oarsman is a rower

explanation.surface: A list of three people: a medic called Ewing, a rower and a vine grower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Ewing' reads as a title and name; doctor is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A viticulturalist cultivates grapevines, which is what a winegrower does.

clue.text: Deaf, poorly and pale

indicators.note: poorly means badly or unwell, so the letters are out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing a sick person: hard of hearing, ill and pallid.
explanation.definitionFit: To pale is to grow faint or lose colour, which is to fade.

clue.text: Light axe

blocks.note: first meaning: to set alight, ignite
second meaning: to dismiss from a job

explanation.walkthrough: 'Light axe' looks like a description of a small hatchet; both words are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire a bonfire is to light it, and to fire an employee is to axe them from the payroll.

clue.text: Back in Reno I nullified my marriage

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words, spanning their join
back means going backwards, so the concealed letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the letters straddling the end of Reno, I and the start of nullified

explanation.surface: Someone got a quick divorce in Reno, Nevada, famous for easy divorces.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining of two people in marriage, a common formal synonym.

clue.text: Force artist, 49, to take course

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
IL is 49 in Roman numerals
a road is a course or route

explanation.surface: An artist aged 49 is compelled to enrol on a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like a noun but is a verb: to railroad someone is to push them into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To railroad a person is to pressure or rush them into acting, so to coerce them.
